reviews.title: Best Budget Case
reviews.comment: One of the best priced cases for what it is. It comes with three ARGB fans at only $50. It looks way more expensive than it is and its a pretty small case which makes the build pc look more solid with not much empty space. The fans are daisy chain-able so I’m planning on adding 4 more fans. Awesome case

reviews.title: FOIFKIN F100 mATX case
reviews.comment: This was my first time buying a brand-new PC case. I originally built my PC in an old Gateway case, but airflow and cooling became an issue, so I decided to upgrade. There isn’t much real-world information on the F100 outside of the Amazon listing, so most of my expectations came from reviews of other Foifkin cases. I expected thin metal, a slightly flimsy top corner above the glass panels, and break-away PCIe covers. The metal is thin and the top corner has some flex on its own, but once the front glass panel is installed it stiffens the case up nicely. I was pleasantly surprised that the PCIe slots use replaceable covers, not break-away ones. Cable management is a bit tight, but that’s expected for a smaller mATX case—especially if you’re using cable extensions and using the HDD mount like I was. I also ran into a minor issue where the 3 different SATA SSD mounts all somewhat conflicted with my PSU’s SATA power cable, but I was able to make it work. If you’re only running an NVMe drive (or NVMe + one SATA drive), cable management should be much easier. The biggest improvement was cooling. Coming from a case with poor-airflow and the stock AMD cooler, pairing this case with a Thermalright 240mm AIO dropped my CPU temperatures by about 10-20°C, which was a huge improvement. Overall, for the price, I’m very happy with this case. It looks good, has solid airflow, and most of the downsides are situational. If you’re on a budget and want a clean-looking mATX case, this is a solid option.
reviews.author: Shad Spendlove
